text: The deviation read that rwb-case consumes is GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations on the S8 rwb-deviation contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout; the approver on each row is composed from the P7 decision log and is optional; a failed read returns deviationsAvailable false with an empty deviations[] and one MSG-GEN-006 entry while the case fields stay in place.
why: The Ownership Map has no GET row for S8 although Architecture v5 slide 15 gives GET/POST /deviations, and the app story cannot contract, fake or test the read without one named path and one degraded shape.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 (S8 IN: GET/POST /deviations); Ownership Map v1 api rows for S8; RWB-ITG-E2015-ITG section 12.2.
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2015-APP 12.2 and flow steps 5 to 7; RWB-P3-E2015-CON 12.2 and AC4; RWB-P3-E2015-OPS 12.2
confirm: Solution architect and the S8 owner, in the baseline review of RWB-P3-E2015-CON.
impact: If S8 publishes another read path or filter, one consumed row, the DeviationClient adapter and one fake change; no schema, event or workflow change.

text: The three operational values are provisional until UAT: the timer projection lag alerts above 5 minutes, the MSG-GEN-006 degradation rate alerts above 1% of case-record reads over 15 minutes, and TimerBreached volume alerts when the hourly count leaves the trailing 7-day band by more than 3 times.
why: No source gives a threshold, a window or a band, and the deployment cannot ship without an alert value; every value stays a values-file entry, never code.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 28 and 44; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; the 2 s read timeout of RWB-E2-015.
confirm: DevOps lead with the rwb-case service owner at UAT, and the platform observability owner for the band definition.
impact: A threshold change is a values-file change and one runbook line; no code, contract or schema change.

text: rwb-case reads the case's interaction-ledger entries through the rwb-source-data contract at a case-scoped read on the rwb-source-data base, one hop with the 2 s timeout and a breaker, and builds the contact item itself; the ledger stays P1's and no interaction table is read or held in rwb_case.
why: The table ruling and the API map disagree on who serves the interaction API, and the map gives no path for the P1 read, so a default is needed for the app story, its fake and the harness.
read: ownership.json api 'GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions' and tables 'interaction'; TSD P3 v3 API-P3-014; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-18
confirm: Architecture review with the P1 and P3 owners before the app story's Done
impact: The eight contact items of AC1, their masked summaries and the INTERACTION type of the timeline

text: The notices of a case are read from the rwb-comms contract as a case-scoped notice list at GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices, carrying id, noticeType, sentDate and deliveryStatus, one hop with the 2 s timeout and a breaker.
why: Architecture v5 slide 17 names the operation for rwb-comms and the Ownership Map has no row for it, so the path and the answer shape must be assumed for the app story, the fake and the harness.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17; Template and Rules R4 (base per service); ownership.json api section
confirm: P6 owner and the solution architect at the wave 2 contract review
impact: The two notice items of AC1, the empty answer of AC8 and the Litigation R filter of AC5

text: The case-side audit read is rwb-case's own operation at GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/rule-change-audit, authorised with the Rules and parameters right R of the legacy report, answering one entry per package version with packageCode, versionLabel, versionStatus, decisions, casesAffected, firstDecisionAt, lastDecisionAt, openCasesAtVersion and openCasesKeepingVersion, in JSON and CSV.
why: The legacy story owns the report and the decisions per version, but the ownership map gives no case-side audit path, so an owner, a path, a right and a shape had to be chosen to keep the case half inside rwb-case.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-041 section 12 and section 16; FSD P3 A2.16; Ownership Map v1 (api block); Architecture v5 slide 41; ASM-A6-tables-3
confirm: Confirm with the solution architect and in the wave 2 API index review before the baseline tag.
impact: If refused, the case-side counts fold into the P7 report and this story keeps only the version pin, the impact count and the refusal guard.

text: This story keeps the rule package version scope of RWB-E2-041 even though the FSD A2.16 examples use a reference-data version and status, because the WP title, the legacy key and every legacy test case are rule packages and the reference-data checklist has its own story.
why: §R3 puts the functional specification above the story masters, so the disagreement has to be resolved explicitly rather than silently.
read: FSD P3 A2.16 AC-P3-016-01 and AC-ALT-P3-016-01; legacy RWB-E2-041 sections 1 to 19; Template and Rules §R3
confirm: Confirm with the business analyst that RWB-E1-043 keeps the reference-data checklist and report.
impact: If the FSD scope is confirmed instead, the report columns and the test data change, and the case-side half of both stories is unaffected.

text: The case-side audit answer and its CSV export are computed on request from rows the service already holds and are not stored as a copy, so their retention follows the retention of the decision records they summarise; the deprecation window of a published field and the retention of the contract fakes stay open.
why: No source fixes these windows, and storing a second copy of case counts would create a second place to keep correct.
read: Architecture v5 slide 28 (records kept where they are written) and slide 29 (own schema only); TSD P3 v3 T2.2; legacy RWB-E2-041 section 17
confirm: Confirm with the data steward against the records retention schedule before wave 2 exit.
impact: If a stored copy is required, one rwb_case summary table and its purge job are added; no contract field changes.

text: The three Epic 2 packages are governed, stored, loaded, approved and promoted in rwb-decision (P7). rwb-case authors the three workbooks and their Tests tabs, fetches the model over GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}, verifies the SHA-256, holds one KieBase per version with a cache of at most 20, swaps atomically, keeps the last good model on failure and reads rule_row only through the catalog. Every registry fact in legacy AC1 to AC6 is proved against the rwb-decision contract mock in RWB-P3-E2042-APP and against the real service in RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG.
why: The ownership ruling ASM-A6-tables-3 and Arch v5 slides 27 and 41 put the registry in rwb-decision, while TSD P3 v3 still declares the tables in the case module; the ACs must be provable on Day 1 without the real registry.
read: Ownership Map v1 (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case; ruling ASM-A6-tables-3); Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slides 27, 41 and 44; Temporal and Drools slides 15 and 16; TSD P3 v3 T2.2 and T3.1; plan split of RWB-E2-042 into RWB-P7-E2042-APP, RWB-P3-E2042-*, RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG
confirm: P7 rwb-decision owner and the solution architect
impact: The registry work, its seed rows, the admin operations, the approval, the rollback and JOB-20 sit in RWB-P7-E2042-APP; the P3 stories keep the workbooks, the model cache, the checksum check, the swap and the payment_match_rule assertion.

text: The model read answers packageCode, versionLabel, checksum (SHA-256), the model content with its compiler version and the valid-from date; the catalog read answers ruleId, packageVersion, drools_rule_name, action_text, owner_role, timer_spec, target_queue_code and outputs; both answer 401, 403, 404 and 503 and are called one hop within a 2 s client budget.
why: No read source fixes the wire shape of the two consumed operations, and the app, infrastructure, operations and test stories need a shape and a fake on Day 1.
read: TSD P3 v3 T2.2 (RuleResult, RuleCatalog.row); Temporal and Drools slide 15 (GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, checksum); Arch v5 slide 27 (evaluate inside an activity, under 300 ms); RWB-P3-E1018-CON consumed-operation table for the error and timeout convention
impact: The element names and the fake are fixed now; the property types, lengths and required flags are settled with the rwb-decision owner before the wave 2 baseline is signed off.

text: The container rule-packages is write-once with no deletion and the reviewed audit retention per environment; each pod is sized by a load test that caches 20 package versions plus its working set at the reviewed heap values; the alert windows, replica counts and probe timings are reviewed values per environment and are not business values.
why: The legacy story states only that the container exists and the identity may read it, and no source gives a retention period, a memory figure, an alert window or a probe timing.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-042 preconditions and section 13; Arch v5 slide 27 (cache, 300 ms target); Temporal and Drools slide 16 (LRU max 20)
confirm: SCB IT infrastructure, the DevOps team and the audit owner
impact: The INF story fixes the policy, the identity and the sizing method; the OPS story fixes the alert names and the runbook entries; the figures are reviewed values and change without a story change.

text: The reference workflow runs on task queue rwb-case in namespace rwb-recovery and carries the legacy evaluate, record, apply order in two activities: EvaluateRulesActivity, then RecordAndApplyActivity, which writes the decision record and the state change in one transaction.
why: The legacy story polls rwb-platform and uses three activities (WriteDecisionLog, ApplyState); the target naming rule gives every service its own queue, and the Temporal and Drools design merges the two write steps into RecordAndApply.
read: Arch v5 Text Extract slides 24 and 41; Temporal and Drools design slide 14; Template and Rules §R4 and §R5.5 DP-03; TSD P3 v3 T2.4 and T2.5
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2043-APP section 7 AC1 note and 12.5; RWB-P3-E2043-CON section 12.5; RWB-P3-E2043-OPS section 12.5
confirm: Solution architect and platform workflow kit owner
impact: Queue, workflow ID, activity names and every Epic 3 workflow copied from the skeleton

text: The synthetic case RW-2026-000777 is a harness-owned fixture seeded only in DEV and SIT, removed after the test, and never carried by a release.
why: The fixture is a precondition of the legacy story with no owner, store or lifecycle; the deployment story needs a rule that keeps it out of UAT and production.

why: Worker versioning and a build ID per worker are required but their format and policy are stated nowhere; the stories need one concrete default.
